title: Determination 2024/012: Whether the installation of a woodburner (on an as-built hearth) complies with the Building Code (clause C2.2)
jurisdiction: New Zealand: Tasman District Council as building consent authority (Richmond); MBIE determination under the Building Act 2004. Non-Alberta comparative record.
code_edition: NZ Building Code (Schedule 1, Building Regulations 1992), clause C2.2 as cited in the record. The manufacturer's hearth-clearance specification is part of the record. No Acceptable Solution edition is named.

facts.text: A woodburner has been installed on an existing as-built hearth at a dwelling in Richmond. The hearth is a necessary element of the installation.
The authority refused to issue a code compliance certificate for the building work and sought a determination on whether the woodburner installation complies with the Building Code.
The question is whether the woodburner on the existing as-built hearth complies with clause C2.2 of the Building Code.
The woodburner has a pedestal or drawer base. The woodburner and hearth combination specification requires a front hearth clearance of 470 mm from the woodburner to a combustible surface.
The record refers to a wood-burner operation guide, and its cross-section shows the woodburner installed on the existing hearth.
The record considers whether the work complies by way of an alternative solution with the performance requirement in clause C2.2.
